messages:
maria: heads up — i pushed a tiny sample app that reproduces a weird case: request-id gets lost / redacted during retries when OTEL hooks are enabled. repo: https://git.internal/repro/reqid-redaction-sample :wave:

maria: repro steps in README, but tl;dr: call endpoint -> observe x-request-id in initial request logs -> trigger an automatic retry -> subsequent logs show no x-request-id (or it shows as <redacted>).

tom: can you paste the minimal logs here?

maria: sure — this is from the sample app (node):

```
INFO 2026-03-20T12:01:02Z http.request "GET /api/foo" headers={"x-request-id":"req-7c3f"}
INFO 2026-03-20T12:01:02Z http.response status=500 body=... retrying
DEBUG 2026-03-20T12:01:02Z retry.middleware "retrying request" attempt=1
INFO 2026-03-20T12:01:02Z http.request "GET /api/foo" headers={"x-request-id":"<redacted>"}
```

maria: the tracer spans still have the trace id, but the header is missing in logs/exporter for the retried request.

leah: i've seen this before — ordering of hooks matters. node SDK attaches the OTEL propagator after the redaction middleware runs in our sample app, whereas python attaches it earlier. parity issue between SDKs. the redaction hook strips sensitive headers too early.

sam: @maria did you try toggling RW_REDACT_HEADERS env?

maria: yes. RW_REDACT_HEADERS=1 reproduces the <redacted> behavior. if i set RW_REDACT_HEADERS=0 the header persists but we then expose potentially PII in logs, which we don't want.

tom: two parallel problems then: (1) req-id gets regenerated/removed during retry construction, (2) redaction runs at a different point relative to otel propagation. we need a deterministic order and a way to preserve request ids for observability while still honoring redaction rules.

leah: quick prototype idea: store x-request-id onto the OTEL span attributes at the moment we first see it, and have the logging wrapper read from span attributes if header missing. that avoids needing the header to survive the whole pipeline.

maria: i pushed a small PR with a repro test and a PoC that copies x-request-id -> span.attr. link: https://git.internal/repro/pull/4

tom: nice. what's the delta across languages? if python already keeps header, we should standardize node/go to match.

leah: python's SDK currently sets up middleware order like: auth -> otel-propagator -> redaction -> logger. node had: auth -> redaction -> otel-propagator -> logger. so node ends up having the header redacted before it reaches the propagator/trace.

sam: can we instead make redaction configurable to run only at log-emission time? i.e. keep sensitive data in in-memory context but apply redaction filter right before writing to disk/exporter.

maria: that's safer. `RW_REDACT_STRATEGY=defer` as an env flag for the sample app shows the behavior we want. i documented it in the README.

infra-bot: deploy preview built for the sample app: https://preview.internal/repro/reqid-redaction (sha: 2f9a7b).

tom: action items:
- leah to audit middleware ordering across node/go/python SDKs and propose a consistent ordering (owner: leah)
- leah to evaluate span-attribute shim for x-request-id as a short-term mitigation
- sam to add CI test in devex/sdks that runs the sample app and asserts x-request-id is present in logs and in exported spans after a retry (owner: sam)
- maria to update onboarding docs + troubleshooting note (owner: maria)

leah: i'll take it. aiming to have a proposal PR by Fri EOD. :eyes:

maria: thanks! i'll update the issue with the logs + steps to repro and link the PR.

sam: sounds good. can we also add a tiny e2e that toggles RW_REDACT_HEADERS in CI matrix so we catch regressions?

devex-bot: created ticket DEVEX-3421 "reqid lost/redacted on retry with OTEL hooks" and linked PRs.

maria: perfect. adding a note to the onboarding sample-app doc so new users don't get tripped up by default log levels/redaction ordering. :thumbsup:
